subject: English
passage: Sociolinguist Shalini Jang believes we might better understand how regional dialects form if we determine why adult speakers sometimes unconsciously adjust their pronunciation — a process called speech accommodation — after brief exposure to unfamiliar speech. Jang and colleagues reviewed data from several earlier studies of how native English speakers respond when exposed to foreign-accented English, including Friedrich Sullivan's work with speakers of Dutch-accented English and Mei Lin Park's work with speakers of Brazilian-accented English. Jang and colleagues concluded that neither Dutch-accented nor Brazilian-accented English is likely to have played a significant role in driving speech accommodation among the listeners.
prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Jang and colleagues' conclusion?

choices.A: Listeners tended to adjust their pronunciation when exposed to Brazilian-accented English, but not when exposed to Dutch-accented English.
choices.B: Listeners tended to adjust their pronunciation when exposed to Dutch-accented English, but not when exposed to Brazilian-accented English.
choices.C: Listeners did not tend to adjust their pronunciation when exposed to either Dutch-accented or Brazilian-accented English.
choices.D: Listeners tended to adjust their pronunciation when exposed to Dutch-accented English and when exposed to Brazilian-accented English.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer. The passage explains that Jang believes understanding why adult speakers sometimes engage in speech accommodation could shed light on how regional dialects form, and that she and her colleagues reviewed studies of how listeners respond when exposed to Dutch-accented and Brazilian-accented English. Their conclusion is that neither of these accented varieties likely played a significant role in driving speech accommodation. A finding that listeners did not tend to adjust their pronunciation when exposed to either variety would directly support this conclusion, since speech accommodation would be the mechanism by which such exposure could contribute to dialect formation.
